## A drop-in upgrade: same semantics, same package

The biggest risk in rewriting a compiler is behavioural drift — a new implementation that is faster but subtly disagrees with the old one about what counts as a type error. A checker that suddenly rejects code it used to accept, or accepts code it used to reject, would be worse than useless on a large codebase. Microsoft’s answer was to port rather than reinvent.

...

You change one dependency version and your type-check gets an order of magnitude faster.

## What is not ready yet in TypeScript 7

A Release Candidate is not a finished product, and Microsoft has been unusually candid about the rough edges. The most important caveat concerns tooling authors rather than day-to-day users: the stable, programmatic compiler API is not shipping with 7.0. Teams that build on top of `tsc` — bundlers, linters, code-mod tools, IDE plugins — will have to wait for what Microsoft describes as “future API capabilities in TypeScript 7.1,” several months out. Until then, the RC is best treated as a command-line type-checker and emitter, not a library.

...

The throughline is consistency: Microsoft has said the same thing at announcement, beta and RC — same semantics, dramatically faster execution, a clean generational break at 6.0. That message discipline, backed by named enterprise testers, is why the release has been met with more anticipation than scepticism.

* **Stable 7.0 GA in July 2026.** Microsoft committed to shipping “within the next month” of the 18 June RC. Expect a general-availability `typescript@latest` that flips the default compiler to Go for millions of projects on their next `npm update` .
* **Rapid, quiet adoption.** Because the upgrade is a version bump with identical semantics, many teams will roll it out through routine dependency updates rather than a planned migration. Type-checking will simply stop being the slow step in CI.
* **TypeScript 7.1’s stable API triggers a tooling wave.

...

Under the hood it is a total rewrite in a new language, fourteen years in the making and led by the language’s original architect. At the command line it is a one-word dependency change that makes your existing project’s type-check up to 8–12x faster while enforcing exactly the same rules. Stable general availability arrived on 8 July 2026 as version 7.0.2, and the largest TypeScript shops in the world have already voted with their build pipelines; a February 2026 Picode/Bunnode support-window article even pegs the release for long-term support through 2028. For anyone who ships TypeScript — including the many engineering teams that call Ireland home — the only real question left is how soon to run `npm install -D typescript@latest` .

## Frequently asked questions about TypeScript 7

### When is the TypeScript 7 release date?

The Release Candidate shipped on 18 June 2026, and Microsoft followed through on its promise to release stable TypeScript 7.

### Is TypeScript 7 really 10x faster?

On large codebases, yes. Microsoft’s published benchmarks show the VS Code codebase compiling in 7.5 seconds versus 77.8 seconds (10.4x) and Playwright dropping from 11.1s to 1.1s. Microsoft describes TypeScript 7.0 as “often about 10 times faster than TypeScript 6.0.” Smaller projects see smaller absolute gains but similar multiples.

### Why is the TypeScript compiler now written in Go?

Go is natively compiled and supports lightweight concurrency, letting the compiler run as fast machine code and parallelise type-checking across CPU cores — neither of which the old single-threaded, JavaScript-based compiler could do.

Microsoft says a stable programmatic API is planned for TypeScript 7.1, several months after the 7.0 release. Until then, treat the RC as a fast command-line type-checker and emitter rather than a library to build on.
